purpose: 横屏宽间隔斜切漫画、羊皮纸底、第一关构图衔接的静态布局对比

variants.label: 五格斜切
variants.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story / reference-guided revision.
Edit the provided earlier comic concept into a NEW polished horizontal 16:9 opening comic layout. This is a static layout concept, all panels visible. One image, not multiple pages, not animation. IMPORTANT priority: noticeably wider parchment gutters and the correct first-level setting.
REFERENCE ROLES, IN THIS ORDER:
Image 1 = previous concept to revise: retain character, painterly quality, cold-dusk atmosphere and opening story, replace its panel geometry/gutters and its incorrect generic palace-garden final scene.
Image 2 = supplied black-outline comic-layout reference: use its oblique polygonal language and separated panels, reinterpret for LANDSCAPE screen. Do not copy portrait orientation, white background, heavy black double borders, text or watermark.
Image 3 = AUTHORITATIVE first game level environment and art reference. The final panel MUST clearly be this specific scene, with recognizable left-to-right geography; see continuity lock below.
Image 4 = AUTHORITATIVE wick-spirit character design reference.
PAGE / GUTTERS: full landscape 16:9 old storybook parchment sheet, pale warm ivory/oatmeal with delicate natural fibers, faint age mottling and subtle slightly darker edges. Restrained storybook age, no burnt edges, no torn scroll ends, no curled scroll, no maps or writing. LARGE open parchment gaps between EVERY panel: approximately 2.4 to 3 percent of total image width, with a generous 3.5 percent outer parchment margin. This must be much more spacious than the previous thin dark gutters. Each separate polygon is edged with a fine single dark-sepia ink outline, NOT thick black strips or doubled black lines. Exposed cream parchment is the dominant visible separator and is clearly seen at all diagonal junctions. Rectangular outer canvas. At least 15 percent of the total surface visibly uncovered parchment. Polygon interiors fully painted, no objects crossing between panels.
ART: beautiful hand-inked translucent watercolor, gently granulated handmade paper, irregular thin linework, detailed ivy and brickwork like Image 3, delicate Gorogoa-like illustrated architecture and LIMBO-like shadow silhouettes. Readable dim cool slate and gray-green environment with small amber highlights. Not a photo, not glossy 3D, not cel-shaded anime faces. Use diagonal comics layout, not anime art style for the character.
CHARACTER LOCK: cream-white thumb-size flame spirit, oversized wind-swept flame head, two long simple dark oval eyes, small mouth, no nose, short small torso/limbs, little golden leaf/flame-shaped chest core. Blue-gray textured shadow patches. Exact reference anatomy, no clothes, no bag, no staff, no carried light, no ears, wings or horns. Very gentle self-glow. Micro-scale in wide shots: a human gate towers over it; a broad ivy leaf is as large as its head or larger; relative size MUST match Image 3's small character. A close-up is camera zoom, not a giant character.
STORY: dusk just BEFORE rain. Tiny spirit walks along an old abandoned wall, pauses at a leaf gap and sees a faint intermittent amber glint on distant greenhouse GLASS, follows it to the garden gate, slips in through an already existing low gap, finds the garden deserted. No rain streaks or downpour. Wind and cloudy sky suggest coming rain. Only one spirit per scene; repeated spirit in different panels is the same character at different times. Greenhouse glint is an ambiguous reflection, never a visible flame or glowing occupied house.
CONTINUITY LOCK FOR FINAL PANEL: reproduce the 2D side-view spatial composition of Image 3, use it as exact visual guide: LEFT EDGE black wrought-iron gate beside a pale weathered rectangular masonry pillar and a few shallow threshold steps; across the middle background a wall of exposed rusty red bricks and patches of cream plaster, vertical pale stone buttresses, trailing ivy, and a large tree canopy arching above. One continuous walkable horizontal moss-covered stone ledge in the foreground. Near center a small antique dark cage-like lantern fixture and tarnished RECTANGULAR tilting mirror mounted to a short masonry post. RIGHT side low uneven steps and the same PALE layered stone/scale-shaped curved mound laid diagonally against their base; far right a broken terracotta pot with a cutout opening and the edge of an old wooden doorway. Use these exact identifiable objects and positions; do not replace the setting with a palace, courtyard fountain, classical urns, grand staircase, or huge greenhouse. The greenhouse is only in distant approach shots, NOT the focus of the final level-sideview shot.
Final-panel spirit stands just inside the LEFT gate, looking RIGHT down that same walkable ledge toward the mirror and steps. The camera is almost orthographic 2D platformer side view, not a path disappearing into the distance. Keep the reference's material colors but adapt it to cloudy evening with a residual muted honey-gold sunset at the canopy and cool shadows. Do not turn it into bright midday. The mirror and pale layered mound are idle: NO solved reflection beam, no glowing scale, no glowing lantern, no awake monster. This is immediately BEFORE gameplay starts.
No dialogue, lettering, numbers, decorative calligraphy, arrows, watermark or UI. Never illustrate the full monster or add people. No title at top. The only frames should be the requested distinct polygon panels.
LAYOUT A / FIVE-PANEL ASYMMETRIC COMIC:
Inside the wide parchment margin, use two irregular wide upper polygons and three unequal lower polygons. The broad inter-row parchment gap rises diagonally from left to right; the other panel cuts run on different oblique angles inspired by the sketch, but keep an obvious reading sequence.
Upper-left wide panel: full tiny spirit walking right along the mossy wall, storm clouds behind leaves.
Upper-right wide panel: spirit in three-quarter closeup looking through a gap in oversized ivy; far greenhouse glint visible beyond.
Bottom-left small oblique panel: low view of the immense rusted gate and tiny spirit arriving.
Bottom-center narrow slanted panel: low close shot of the spirit carefully stepping through the pre-existing gap beneath the gate, not pushing the enormous gate.
Bottom-right LARGE landscape polygon, approximately half of the lower row: the specific first-level environment from Image 3 and tiny spirit on the left entry ledge. Fit the left gate, center mirror, right scale-mound and terracotta pot in that landscape panel without cropping away the recognisable landmarks.
The final panel is about twice the area of either other bottom panel. Avoid a rigid grid, preserve lively diagonal edges and especially wide CREAM PARCHMENT channels. The mood should resemble a carefully illustrated aged storybook page, not black-bordered screen tiles.
